title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus invalid-pch error on shared cmake_pch.hxx.gch
signature: cc1plus: error: cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API step fails: cc1plus reports cmake_pch.hxx.gch is not a valid PCH file, -Werror=invalid-pch turns it fatal

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Check status of all jobs step fails because the upstream Build / Build job failed

key_errors: cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
root_cause: During the 'CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API' step, the same build directory (openvino_build) is reconfigured in-place with 'cmake -UTBB* ... -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TBB=OFF -DENABLE_WHEEL=OFF' and rebuilt with ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD precompiled headers enabled. The reconfigure changes compiler flags/defines for openvino_reference without invalidating or regenerating the previously-built cmake_pch.hxx.gch, so cc1plus rejects the stale .gch as 'not a PCH file'. Because CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR/-Werror=invalid-pch is on, this normally-recoverable PCH mismatch becomes a hard build failure. This is a recurring CI configuration/caching issue (9 prior occurrences since 2026-09-25) tied to how the JS API build step reuses the main build tree's PCH artifacts rather than a regression introduced by this commit.
reproduction_steps: Locally: 1) Configure and build openvino for Linux_aarch64 cross-compilation with ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=ON (precompiled headers), 2) Without a clean build dir, reconfigure the same build dir with 'cmake -UTBB* -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TBB=OFF -DENABLE_WHEEL=OFF' (the JS API step in job_build_linux.yml), 3) Run 'cmake --build' again; cc1plus will reject the previously generated cmake_pch.hxx.gch as invalid once source flags changed.
recommended_actions: In .github/workflows/job_build_linux.yml, force regeneration of precompiled headers for the JS API reconfigure step (e.g., rm the affected *_pch.hxx.gch / *.dir trees, or disable ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD for that reconfigured build) instead of reusing the shared build directory in place.
Alternatively, use a separate build directory for the OpenVINO JS API cmake/npm build so it does not share a PCH-enabled object tree with the main build.
Downgrade -Werror=invalid-pch to a warning for this specific reconfigure step, or pass -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF when invoking the JS API build.
Since this has recurred 9+ times since 2026-09-25, escalate to the build/CI owners of job_build_linux.yml rather than treating as a one-off.
prevention_strategies: Avoid reconfiguring/rebuilding an already-PCH-populated build directory with different compiler flags in place; always use a clean or dedicated build directory per CMAKE_COMPILE flag-set, or explicitly invalidate stale .gch files before a flag-changing reconfigure. Add a CI guard that detects and removes stale precompiled header artifacts whenever CPACK_GENERATOR or ENABLE_* cmake options change between successive cmake invocations in the same build tree.
historical_context: This exact signature has been observed 9 times since 2026-09-25T10:37:07Z, always in the ARM64 cross-compilation post-commit build, always in the OpenVINO JS API reconfigure/build step of job_build_linux.yml. No fix has landed yet; recommend prioritizing a permanent fix (separate build dir or PCH invalidation) given the recurrence rate.
